title: Chilli Crab
subtitle: Singaporean crab in spiced tomato and egg sauce
excerpt: Singapore's national dish: whole mud crab or brown crab stir-fried and finished in a rich, sweet, savoury sauce of chilli, tomato, garlic, and egg, poured thickly over the crab in the shell. Messy, sociable, and unlike anything else.

recipe.sourceNotes: Chilli crab was created in Singapore in 1956 by Cher Yam Tian, who added a sweet and spicy tomato sauce to a basic stir-fried crab she had been making for years. It was subsequently popularised and refined by her husband's seafood restaurant and eventually became recognised as Singapore's unofficial national dish. The defining sauce combines fresh and dried chillies with tomato sauce, Chinese rice wine or Shaoxing, soy sauce, and eggs stirred in at the end to create a slightly thickened, flowing sauce. The sauce should be sweet, sour, and hot simultaneously; mantou (Chinese steamed buns) are the traditional accompaniment for mopping up the sauce.

content.text: Ask the fishmonger to dispatch and clean the crab for you, and have them chop it into pieces through the shell. The crab cooks through in the wok in the sauce; it does not need to be cooked beforehand. Have all the sauce ingredients ready before you start: the wok works fast. The eggs are stirred in off the heat at the very end and should form light ribbons in the sauce.

items.preparation: use 2 whole blue swimmer crabs or 1 whole brown crab, cleaned and chopped through the shell into pieces

content.text: Mix the tomatoes, soy sauce, sugar, and vinegar in a bowl. Heat the oil in a wok over the highest heat. Stir-fry the crab pieces for 3 to 4 minutes until the shells begin to colour. Remove and set aside.

Add the garlic, ginger, and chilli to the wok. Stir-fry for 30 seconds. Add the tomato sauce mixture and 100 ml of water. Return the crab, turning to coat. Cover and cook for 5 to 6 minutes, tossing occasionally, until the crab is cooked through.

Remove the wok from the heat. Pour the beaten egg in a thin stream over the crab, stirring gently; it should form light egg ribbons in the sauce. Season. Transfer to a large bowl and scatter with spring onion and coriander. Serve with bread to mop up the sauce.
